resonanceScreen.status: Review - Plain shunt bank resonates near 7th harmonic
Review - Plain shunt bank resonates near 7th harmonic

detuningJustification.problem: At higher stages (350 - 400 kVAr), a plain shunt capacitor bank creates parallel resonance order hr = 6.87 - 7.34, dangerously close to the 7th harmonic (420 Hz). VFDs and nonlinear loads would excite excessive harmonic resonance.
detuningJustification.solution: 7% series detuned reactors shift the series LC resonance frequency to fr = f1 / sqrt(0.07) = 60 / 0.2646 = 226.78 Hz (harmonic order 3.78). This sits cleanly below the 5th harmonic (300 Hz) and prevents harmonic amplification.
detuningJustification.feederWarning: Central APFC relieves upstream transformer and main bus current, but does NOT reduce reactive current in the individual floor feeders (F1 to F6).

year0.verdict: NEGATIVE ENERGY-ONLY PAYBACK at present load. Internal reactor losses (5 W/kVAr) exceed upstream I²R savings.

year10.verdict: Long simple payback (116.7 years). Justification is technical compliance, voltage support, and transformer thermal release, NOT bill savings.
